subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: Is current source-level main OAuth inheritance sufficient to close #87051, or should it stay open until a maintainer-run live `sessions_spawn` Codex OAuth proof covers the reported production path?
rationale: The central code path now has source and unit-test support, but the report is security-sensitive and the exact channel/cron subagent fallback path still lacks live proof while adjacent `agentDir` propagation evidence remains open.

options.title: Keep open for live proof
options.body: Require a current-main live or Crabbox-backed `sessions_spawn` Codex OAuth run showing no auth fallback before closing.

options.title: Close after maintainer proof
options.body: If a maintainer already has equivalent live proof, close as implemented on main with that proof and the main-only commit timestamp.

options.title: Split residual agentDir work
options.body: Close only the inherited OAuth part and move the remaining background/tool `agentDir` propagation or fallback-warning behavior to narrower canonical issues.

recommendation.title: Keep open for live proof
recommendation.body: Require a current-main live or Crabbox-backed `sessions_spawn` Codex OAuth run showing no auth fallback before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The related QA-Lab Codex auth proof and closure history make this the strongest maintainer-facing owner signal for the proof-sufficiency decision.
